name: Trinity College Dublin
description: Ireland’s oldest university holds the Book of Kells exhibition in its Old Library.

name: Rock of Cashel
description: Medieval church ruins crown a limestone outcrop above Tipperary farmland.

name: Kilmainham Gaol
description: A former prison museum covering Irish independence history on Dublin’s west side.

name: Newgrange
description: A prehistoric passage tomb aligned to the winter solstice sunrise in the Boyne Valley.

name: O’Brien’s Tower
description: A 19th-century tower stands on the cliff edge at the Cliffs of Moher walkways.

name: Cliffs of Moher
description: Sheer Atlantic cliffs run for kilometres with marked coastal paths.

name: Ring of Kerry
description: A scenic driving loop around the Iveragh Peninsula with mountain and coastal views.

name: Skellig Michael
description: A remote monastic island of steep steps and beehive huts off the Kerry coast (boat access weather-dependent).

name: Dingle Peninsula
description: Coastal roads, early Christian sites and harbour towns on County Kerry’s peninsula.

name: Connemara National Park
description: Bog, mountain and coast landscapes in County Galway with waymarked trails.

name: Temple Bar food streets
description: Restaurants and pubs pack Dublin’s cultural quarter — lively and tourist-heavy.

name: English Market
description: A covered Victorian market in Cork sells produce, seafood and prepared foods.

name: Galway Market
description: Weekend stalls by St. Nicholas’ Collegiate Church sell crafts and street food.

name: Moore Street Market
description: A historic street market north of the Liffey selling fruit, vegetables and flowers.

name: Killarney town eateries
description: Gateway town to Killarney National Park with pubs serving Irish classics.

name: St Patrick’s Day Festival
description: Parades and city-wide celebrations mark Ireland’s national day each 17 March.
